purpose: Every dimension svc evaluates a build on, how each is measured, and where the standard comes from. Hidden tests cover correctness; this registry covers the rest: what makes software production-ready, what makes it lean rather than slop or over-built, and what makes it good to use. Prefer the cheapest grader that fits: a deterministic probe first, a judge only for what cannot be computed, and a judge rubric made of checkable claims, not a 1-5 scale.

classes.gate: Mandatory for production. Any failure blocks a release, whatever the other scores.
classes.quality: Engineering quality. Compared between arms on the same task; lower or higher is better as stated.
classes.efficiency: Cost and speed, of the build and of the running product.
classes.taste: Product and design quality a user feels. Judged blind, from screenshots and use, with named claims.

sources.mutation-testing: DeMillo, Lipton and Sayward, Hints on Test Data Selection (1978); Papadakis et al., Mutation Testing Advances (2019)

dimensions.measure: hidden tests
judge: journeys specified and covered by a passing test
judge claim: every route and form validates and rejects bad input at the boundary
judge claim + planted probes (review-security pillar): no route acts on another user's data
probe: secrets.hardcoded
judge claim: errors return a structured body, never a stack trace
judge claim: replayed webhooks and concurrent refunds pay out once
judge claim: secrets and endpoints come from the environment
judge claim: README states setup, configuration, run, test and deploy
probe: mutation.score (share of seeded source mutations the build's own tests catch)
probe: tests.trivial + tests.skipped
hidden tests on inputs absent from visible tests; judge claim: no value hard-coded for a test input
probe: size.source_loc and size.source_files, compared between arms on the same task at equal correctness
probe: slop.unused_exports
probe: slop.empty_catch
probe: slop.todo_or_placeholder
probe: size.duplicated_line_share
probe: size.dependencies
judge claim: nothing built that the request and its journeys do not need (no speculative config, plugin layers or abstractions with one use)
judge claim: domain rules importable and testable without HTTP or UI; for games, simulation importable without a DOM
run: cost_usd
run: wall_ms
browser probe: p95 frame interval under 20 ms while playing
browser probe: page interactive
browser probe: no page or console errors while used
judge claims from screenshots: avoids the named default styles (cream background, italic accent words, 01/02/03 labels, monospace labels, pill buttons); a deliberate palette and type scale
judge claims: labelled controls, keyboard operable, visible focus, readable contrast
judge claims: loading, empty, error and success states exist and say what to do next
probe: same seed and inputs give the same state
probe: scripted and random bots play many seeded games: no exception, no NaN, no softlock
judge claims: a clear goal, a decision every few seconds, a fail state and a reason to replay
judge claims: difficulty rises over a run; new elements appear after the first minute
judge claims from screenshots and play: every player action has visible feedback (hit flash, particles, shake, sound or tween)
judge claims: how to play is shown in the first screen; pause, restart and a readable HUD
judge claims from screenshots: a coherent palette and shapes, not default rectangles on black
